spec_match.rationale: The demos are built directly on HTML's update-the-rendering ordering: animations are updated and their events sent before the animation frame callbacks run, so a frame counter installed when a transition is created reads zero if the event was dispatched at the first opportunity and one if an iteration was skipped. That inference is asserted in the conformance suite rather than assumed, because every number on these pages depends on it.

interactive.rationale: Five trigger points measured with a repetition control and medians; a recorded sequence of one breakpoint crossing with per-entry frame numbers and the spec's step list marked with what was observed; and a slider that times every breakpoint crossing, with a ten-pass sweep.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index says there is no new API here and that interoperability is the whole feature, which is the ChromeStatus entry's own framing, and it states plainly that the demos can only show the pre-change state on a Chrome 150.

edge_cases.rationale: Triggers from outside the rendering steps as well as inside; a 20-frame timeout that reports 'no transition ran' rather than hanging; and the reset problem that a style change to reset a transitioning property creates a transition of its own — handled by suppressing transitions across the reset, which is what made the measurements meaningful.

references.rationale: chromestatus.com/feature/6312504658624512 on the index and all three concept pages, with the HTML event loop processing model, CSS Transitions, and MDN.

conformance.rationale: Six immutable assertions: the event exists and carries its property, MediaQueryList is an EventTarget, transitionrun precedes transitionstart, animation events precede animation frame callbacks (the ordering every measurement rests on), and the two cases the change is about — a transition created in a media query listener and one created in a scroll handler must both be dispatched in the same rendering iteration. The last two are expected to fail before Chrome 153 and pass after, which is the point of recording them now.

runtime_evidence.rationale: deno task drive over all three pages in real Chrome 150: 3/3, 20 assertions. Measured, and consistent across pages: a transition started from a media query change listener or a scroll handler arrives one rendering iteration late, while one started from a microtask or an animation frame callback arrives at the first opportunity. The breakpoint sweep recorded 9 crossings, 0 of them in the same iteration. Running with --enable-experimental-web-platform-features produced identical numbers, confirming there is no flag for this.

telemetry_health.rationale: Each page emits showcaseTelemetry.assert with the measured frame counts, the recorded entry count, and the on-time ratio.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, no raw colour literals, buttons set background and colour, 44px minimums including the range input, wide tables in their own scroll containers, and the stage iframe carries a title.

accessibility.rationale: Every iframe has a title describing what it is for; results are announced through aria-live; verdicts are sentences containing the measured numbers rather than colour alone; the recorded sequence is a semantic table with row headers.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: The stage frames are width:100% (or width-constrained inside an overflow-x container on the breakpoint page, where the width is the variable being demonstrated); fact grids are auto-fit minmax; the record tables scroll inside their own containers.

openQuestions.title: Re-measure on Chrome 153 and record the change
openQuestions.detail: This is the rare feature where the before state is the only one observable on the build available, and there is no flag to see the after. The pages are written to read correctly in both worlds, and the conformance suite's last two assertions are written to flip from fail to pass. Re-running the drive spec on 153 and comparing the numbers is the completion of this work, not an extra.

openQuestions.title: Explain the two-frame gap on the event-order page
openQuestions.detail: frames-to-run measures the media query case at one iteration late, while event-order recorded the change at frame 1 and transitionrun at frame 3. The pages report what they measured rather than reconciling the two, which is honest but unsatisfying: the likely cause is that the resize of the parent's iframe element and the child's own rendering iteration are not the same iteration, so one of those frames is the width change reaching the child rather than a dispatch delay. Worth isolating with a resize that happens inside the child.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive iframe stage that can be resized across a breakpoint without page overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Keep deliberately-wide or width-driven content inside its own overflow container so changing its width never widens the page.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The breakpoint page's iframe is the one element whose width is the variable under test, so it lives in an overflow-x:auto wrapper; the other two stages are width:100% and shrink with the column.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: responsive-check desktop + mobile on the feature.

guidanceConsulted.query: announce measured results from a timed run in a live region
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Give every asynchronous measurement a text result in a live region, and disable the control that starts it while it runs.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: All three pages write a narrative verdict into an aria-live output; the measure and sweep buttons disable themselves for the duration and re-enable in every exit path including the timeout.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: deno task drive waits on the verdict text on each page and asserts its content.

summary: Three concepts that measure a timing bug rather than describing it. The build's own reset code created the transition it was trying to time — fixing that was what turned nonsense milliseconds into a clean, repeatable result: on Chrome 150, transitions started inside the rendering steps are dispatched one iteration late, and transitions started outside them are not. The conformance suite records that as two assertions expected to flip when 153 lands.
